findings.title: Same-document contradiction: injectedNotAmbient still says ExecutionId is content-derived
findings.detail: executionCoreBoundary.injectedNotAmbient[ID source].resolution: 'RunId/ExecutionId are content-derived or supplied.' LN-13: ExecutionId is attempt-unique and must differ for identical inputs; only RunId/EvidenceDigest are content-derived. The repair fixed the test and left the boundary prose wrong — next implementer will re-break LN-13 by reading the boundary table.
findings.requiredFix: Rewrite ID injection note: ExecutionId = unique attempt id from injected source; RunId/EvidenceDigest = content-derived (or host policy). Never 'ExecutionId content-derived'.

findings.title: LN-11 closure-at-link-graph is not achievable as written with StoreHandle; boundary must be interface-scoped
findings.detail: Author peerReviewRequired already asks this. Independent view: a core that links a sqlite/CAS implementation has filesystem symbols in the import graph. LN-11 as 'import/call closure reaches no filesystem API' fails for any real store. Without scoping closure to 'core package + deps except behind StoreHandle/provider ports', LN-11 is either vacuous (exclude everything) or impossible (include store). LN-12 runtime denial is the load-bearing half; LN-11 needs a port-boundary definition to be non-vacuous.
findings.requiredFix: Define LN-11 allowlist: only StoreHandle, snapshotAccess, providerRegistry, scheduler ports may touch FS/net/spawn; core modules' static closure excluding those adapters must be clean. Document how providers that spawn rustc are outside the core (supervisor) vs inside (forbidden).

findings.title: providerRegistry vs explicitlyAbsent process-spawn tension under semantic providers
findings.detail: Core does fact derivation and holds providerRegistry, yet explicitlyAbsent bans process spawn. Real TS/Rust semantic providers often require process or in-process compiler APIs (TCB). If providers run in-process linked, spawn/FS may appear in closure. If providers are host-supervised outside the core, fact-derivation is not fully 'inside' the core — the boundary definition ('fact derivation inside') conflicts. Same class as Error 2 if we pretend registry injection is a capability boundary.
findings.requiredFix: State: providers execute only through scheduler/supervisor ports; core never links compiler FS; or accept providers as TCB-inside and narrow LN-11/explicitlyAbsent accordingly with honesty.
